newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Jan core prices slip to 7.5% y/y - economist.
newsitem.headline: Greek Jan core prices slip to 7.5% y/y - economist.

text.p: Greece's January core inflation eased to 7.5 percent year-on-year from December's 7.7 percent, based on the revised consumer price index (CPI) introduced in January, an economist at a foreign bank told Reuters.
Core inflation excludes volatile food and energy prices.
Revised October core inflation stood at 6.7 percent year-on-year, down from November's 7.5 percent, he said.

This means core inflation fell less than headline inflation, which dropped sharply to 6.8 percent year-on-year in January from December's 7.3 percent. Lower fresh fruit and vegetable prices and smaller rises in motor fuel and heating oil prices contributed much to the 0.3-percent month-on-month decline in headline inflation, according to the data.
Good weather helped boost fruit and vegetable supplies this year.
Milder northern hemisphere temperatures depressed heating oil demand prices and increased supplies of Iraqi crude have crushed oil's winter rally and drove crude prices lower.

Drachma-denominated energy prices are determined by world oil prices and the dollar/drachma rate. The National Statistics Service does not release core inflation figures, but it is known that the central bank and the national economy ministry track it. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
